text:
Jia: Putting all Celeste on-prem postmortem follow-ups in one thread so we can track owners + dates. Root postmortem attached to the doc — this is focused on remediation/actions only.

Tom: thanks — quick summary of the three recurring failure modes we saw: VPC peering flaps during bursts, on-prem firewall rules blocking ephemeral ports, and an isolation bug in the dedicated tenant routing table.

Marta: +1. I've started a spreadsheet but we should keep action items here too. I can take ownership of the peering checklist if nobody else volunteers.

Ryan: I can own the firewall changes with infra; need to validate customer change window and whether their change control accepts our proposed rule. ETA: next Wed (2026-04-08).

Samir: I'll take the isolation bug in routing. Repro steps are in the postmortem; root cause is a race in the tenant sync job when BGP sessions flap. Short patch is ready, longer fix needs integration tests.

Jia: great. Let's make the items explicit. ACTION: Marta - validate cross-account peering config + add a quick healthcheck runbook (due 2026-04-02).

Jia: ACTION: Ryan - coordinate with Celeste infra to schedule firewall window and push updated whitelist rules + run verification tests (due 2026-04-08).

Jia: ACTION: Samir - land routing sync guard (hotfix) in staging, run chaos test for BGP session churn, and follow with integration fix PR (hotfix due 2026-03-30, full PR due 2026-04-15).

Tom: For peering healthcheck, suggest we add the following quick test to the runbook so customer ops can run it from their side:
```
# from customer VLAN to Redwood peering IPs
for ip in 10.240.1.1 10.240.1.2; do
  ping -c 3 $ip || echo "peer $ip unreachable"
done
```

Marta: I'll add that and a vendor-facing checklist (what to escalate to support vs what to open a ticket for).

Samir: On the routing bug, Jack in infra flagged that our tenant-sync uses a best-effort backoff that can starve updates when BGP resets happen frequently. I'll add a lock + idempotent replay to avoid partial state.

Ryan: For firewall verification, I plan to run: 
```
iperf3 -c 10.2.1.5 -p 5201 -t 10
curl -sS http://10.2.1.5:8080/health || echo health-fail
```
We'll paste outputs to the ticket.

Jia: Good. Two other administrative items: (1) add these actions to the customer remediation board (I will create tickets), (2) set weekly check-in for 30 min until all actions closed. Proposed cadence: Mondays 11:00 PT.

Tom: Can we add an alert on our side for repeated peering BGP flaps >3 times in 10m for a specific customer? That would catch the pattern earlier.

Marta: yes — I can add a per-customer signal to the peering monitor. Will add as a follow-up task: ACTION: Marta - implement BGP chirp alert + dashboard (due 2026-04-09).

Samir: If we add that alert, we should also add an automated snapshot collector that pulls route table + tenant-sync logs for the 15 minutes around the flap. That'll speed triage. ACTION: Samir - snapshot collector (due 2026-04-12).

Ryan: Noted. Once we have the snapshot, I can run the firewall correlation to see if packets were dropped or never sent.

Incident-bot: Reminder: weekly follow-up meeting scheduled by Jia at 2026-03-30T18:00:00Z (calendar invite sent).

Jia: I'll track the tickets and post progress here each Monday. Please update the ticket when you hit blockers. If any ETA slips, ping me in-channel with a reason so I can update the customer.

Marta: Added initial ticket IDs: REM-4123 (peering healthchecks), REM-4124 (BGP alert), REM-4125 (peering runbook). I'll link PRs as they land.

Samir: Hotfix PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/678 - testing in staging now.

Ryan: Firewall ticket REM-4130 opened and shared with Celeste ops. Customer confirmed change window 2026-04-07 02:00-04:00 UTC.

Jia: Summary for handoff: owners + due dates in the thread above. I'll close this Slack thread once all REM tickets are closed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
